results.content: MOMA-AC: A PREFERENCE-DRIVEN ACTOR-CRITIC FRAMEWORK FOR CONTINUOUS MULTI-OBJECTIVE MULTI-AGENT REINFORCEMENT LEARNING Adam Callaghan University of Galway Galway Ireland H91 TK33 Karl Mason University of Galway Galway Ireland H91 TK33 Patrick Mannion University of Galway Galway Ireland H91 TK33 ABSTRACT This paper addresses a critical gap in Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MOMARL) by introducing the first dedicated inner-loop actor–critic framework for con-tinuous state and action spaces: Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Actor–Critic (MOMA-AC). The framework combines a multi-headed actor network, a centralised critic, and an objective preference-conditioning architecture, enabling a single neural network to encode the Pareto front of optimal trade-off policies for all agents across conflicting objectives in a continuous MOMARL setting. Through comprehensive empirical evaluations, we demonstrate that MOMA-AC consistently outperforms two conventional baselines: a decentralised variant in which each agent independently trains a multi-objective TD3 policy, and an outer-loop baseline in which MA-TD3 [13] is applied iteratively across a sequence of fixed scalarisation weights. We introduce MOMA-AC, the first inner-loop multi-objective multi-agent RL framework designed specifically for continuous state and action spaces, capable of approximating Pareto fronts via scalarisation-based training. Algorithms such as MO-AIM [41] and MOAVOA-MADDPG [37] extend learning to continuous-action MOMA frameworks for asynchronous agents; however, their outer-loop nature requires training separate policies for fixed preferences, lacking a unified, preference-conditioned solution capable of covering the Pareto front in a single training run. MOMA-AC integrates CTDE, preference-conditioned policies, vector-valued rewards, and utility-based optimisation to learn a diverse set of solutions aligned with user-defined objectives for a team of co-operative agents. 9 Algorithm 1 Training Procedure for MOMA-TD3 1: Initialise environment E with n agents 2: Initialise multi-headed actor network πϕ 3: Initialise centralised critics Qθ1, Qθ2 4: Initialise target networks: π ¯ ϕ, Q¯ θ1 and Q¯ θ2 5: Initialise replay buffers Di for each agent i 6: Set hyperparameters: γ, τ, σ, policy_freq, batch_size 7: for episode = 1 to M do 8: Sample preference vector ω0 ∼U(0, 1) 9: Reset environment, receive initial observations o = (o1, o2, ..., on) 10: while episode not terminated do 11: for each agent i do 12: Pad oi to uniform dimension 13: Select action ai = πi,ϕ(oi, ω) + ϵi, ϵi ∼N(0, σ2) 14: end for 15: Execute joint action a = (a1, .

results.content: # MOMA-AC: A preference-driven actor-critic framework for continuous multi-objective multi-agent reinforcement learning. The first inner-loop Multi-Objective Multi-Agent framework capable of handling continuous state and action spaces. This paper addresses a critical gap in Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MOMARL) by introducing the first dedicated inner-loop actor–critic framework for continuous state and action spaces: Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Actor–Critic (MOMA-AC). The framework combines a multi-headed actor network, a centralised critic, and an objective preference-conditioning architecture, enabling a single neural network to encode the Pareto front of optimal trade-off policies for all agents across conflicting objectives in a continuous MOMARL setting. These results establish our framework as a foundational step towards robust, scalable multi-objective policy learning in continuous multi-agent domains. To bridge the methodological gap in MOMARL, we propose MOMA-AC, the first inner-loop actor–critic framework specifically designed for continuous state and action spaces that unifies multi-objective optimisation with multi-agent coordination. Through comprehensive empirical evaluations, we demonstrate that MOMA-AC consistently outperforms two conventional baselines: a decentralised variant in which each agent independently trains a multi-objective TD3 policy, and an outer-loop baseline in which MA-TD3 [13] is applied iteratively across a sequence of fixed scalarisation weights. We introduce MOMA-AC, the first inner-loop multi-objective multi-agent RL framework designed specifically for continuous state and action spaces, capable of approximating Pareto fronts via scalarisation-based training. In this section we introduce MOMA-AC, the first multi-agent actor-critic framework designed for continuous control in multi-objective environments. MOMA-AC integrates CTDE, preference-conditioned policies, vector-valued rewards, and utility-based optimisation to learn a diverse set of solutions aligned with user-defined objectives for a team of co-operative agents. This work introduces MOMA-AC, to our knowledge the first dedicated inner-loop actor–critic framework for continuous multi-objective multi-agent reinforcement learning. ### A novel multi-objective optimization based multi-agent deep reinforcement learning approach for microgrid resources planning. ### Multi-agent reinforcement learning: a review of challenges and applications. ### Automated driving highway traffic merging using deep multi-agent reinforcement learning in continuous state-action spaces. ### A multi-objective multi-agent deep reinforcement learning approach to residential appliance scheduling. His main research interests are in the areas of reinforcement learning, multi-objective decision making and multi-agent systems.
